label: Ridgeline Native Full Audit
changes: Layers > Topographic overlays: 'Hunting permit areas' checkbox (off by default) with a dashed blaze-orange key.

Served live from DOC, nothing bundled: each data tile (zoom 8, 11 or 13 by camera zoom) is one query to DOC's ArcGIS service 'DOC Recreational Hunting Areas' (item 2142c60984cb4a4887ed189662bec148) in tile mode, PBF, generalised to 1/1024 of the tile width; only HuntStatus = 'Permitted' (DOC asks that external distribution be of permitted areas only). Typically 2-30 KB per tile. Requests go through the map transport and HTTP cache; DOC's 30 s cache lifetime is extended to a day for these tiles only.
Drawn with the existing overlay pipeline (draped on 3D terrain, in PDFs only via the map tiles they are not): dashed blaze-orange outlines from zoom 7, area names from zoom 11.

Tap inside an area (when not drawing a route): its name, type, permit area, size and a link to DOC's permit and conditions page, with DOC's caveat (guide only, not legal boundaries, a DOC permit is needed). Overlapping areas (e.g. a roar block inside a permit area) are all listed.
Credit: 'Hunting permit areas: Department of Conservation · CC BY 4.0' in the map credits and About text; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES updated.
dataChecks: Decoder checked against DOC's full-detail GeoJSON: decoded vertices within about 6 m of DOC's outline at a 9.6 m generalisation; the app's exact request URL returns HTTP 200 application/x-protobuf from DOC.

tests.kotlinJvm: 215 tests, 0 failures (new: HuntingAreasTest x4 on real DOC tile responses)
